citations.quote:
Medically Necessary means any treatment, tests, medication, or stay in Hospital or part of a stay in
Hospital which
 is required for the medical management of the Illness or Injury suffered by the ins ured;
 must not exceed the level of care necessary to provide safe, adequate and appropriate medical
care in scope, duration, or intensity;
 must have been prescribed by a Medical Practitioner,
 must conform to the professional standards widely accepted in i nternational medical practice or
by the medical community in India.

citations.claim: A 30-day waiting period applies to all claims unless the insured has continuous coverage from the previous policy year or at least 1 year of continuous coverage under another Indian insurer's policy.
citations.section: WHAT WE EXCLUDE / 2. 30 days Waiting Period
citations.quote:
2. 30 days Waiting Period
A waiting period of 30 days will apply to all claims unless:
 You have been insured under this Policy continuously and without any break in the previous Policy Year,
or
 You were insured continuously and without interruption for at least 1 year under any other Indian
insurer's individual health insurance Policy for the reimbursement of medical costs for inpatient
treatment in a Hospital, and You establish to Our satisfaction that You were unaware of and had not taken
any advice or medication for such Illness or treatment.
 If You renew with Us or transfer from any other insurer and increase the Sum Insured (other than as a
result of the application of Cumulative Bonus upon Renewal with Us, then this exclusion shall only apply
in relation to the amount by which the Sum Insured has been increased.

semantic_checks.explanation: The cited excerpt confirms the definition of a hospital requires registration under the Clinical Establishments Act, 2010, or compliance with specific minimum criteria.

The cited excerpt defines Medically Necessary as treatment required for medical management, not exceeding necessary care levels, prescribed by a practitioner, and conforming to professional standards.

The policy states a 30-day waiting period applies unless the insured has continuous coverage from the previous policy year or at least 1 year of continuous coverage under another Indian insurer's policy.
The cited excerpts confirm coverage for pre-hospitalization (30 days) and post-hospitalization (60 days) expenses, provided the inpatient claim is admissible.
The case facts do not provide evidence of hospital registration or compliance with the minimum criteria defined in the policy.
The policy limits normal room expenses to 1.0% of the Basic Sum Insured (500,000 * 0.01 = 5,000).
The policy limits medical practitioner fees to 25% of the Sum Assured (500,000 * 0.25 = 125,000).
The policy limits medicines and diagnostics to 40% of the Sum Insured (500,000 * 0.40 = 200,000).
The policy limits ambulance charges to 1.0% of the Basic Sum Insured (5,000) or Rs 1,000, whichever is less (1,000).
